title: Southeast Asia Digital Nomad Visa Comparison
description: Compare digital nomad and remote worker visa options across Southeast Asia. Each country offers different requirements, durations, and benefits for location-independent professionals.
disclaimer: This comparison is compiled from publicly available sources for general reference only. Visa requirements change frequently. Always verify current requirements directly with each country's immigration authority before applying. This is not immigration consulting or legal advice.

data.visaCategory: Multiple-entry non-immigrant visa (workcation / digital nomad visa). Covers remote work, soft power activities, and medical treatment.
data.extensionRules: Multiple entries permitted within 5-year validity. Each entry allows up to 180 days. Can extend once per entry for an additional 180 days at local immigration office (THB 1,900 fee).
data.financialRequirement: THB 500,000 (~USD 15,000) in savings, or proof of foreign income
data.incomeProof: Bank statements or payslips showing foreign income
data.healthInsurance: Not a national DTV requirement. Some embassies may request travel insurance at their discretion.
data.remoteWorkAllowed: Yes — can work for foreign companies and freelance for non-Thai clients
data.localWorkAllowed: No — cannot work for Thai companies or obtain Thai work permit
data.applicationFee: THB 10,000 (~USD 300) via e-visa system. Exact USD amount varies by embassy and exchange rate.
data.dependents: Yes — spouses and unmarried children under 20
data.taxImplications: Tax resident if staying >180 days/year. As of Jan 1, 2024: all foreign income remitted to Thailand is taxable for tax residents, regardless of when earned. Income earned before Jan 1, 2024 is exempt under grandfather clause (Revenue Dept instruction Por.162/2566). Consult a Thai tax advisor.
data.recentChanges: Launched July 2024. Full e-visa system from January 2025. Visa run enforcement tightened November 2025 for visa-exempt entries (does not apply to DTV holders).

data.officialName: E33G Visa Pekerja Jarak Jauh (Remote Worker Visa)
data.visaCategory: Visa Tinggal Terbatas / Limited Stay Visa (Indonesia's digital nomad visa)
data.extensionRules: Renewable annually online. After ITAS conversion, obtain MERP (Multiple Exit Re-Entry Permit) for international travel. Leaving without MERP may invalidate the permit.
data.financialRequirement: USD 60,000 minimum annual income from foreign employer, plus USD 2,000 savings in last 3 months
data.incomeProof: Employment contract with foreign company and bank statements
data.healthInsurance: Not listed as an official requirement. Private healthcare widely available.
data.remoteWorkAllowed: Yes — must work for foreign employer (mandatory requirement)
data.localWorkAllowed: No — cannot work for Indonesian companies or accept local employment
data.applicationFee: IDR 7,000,000 (~USD 450) total (includes VITAS, verification, and ITAS fees). MERP (Multiple Exit Re-Entry Permit) is a separate fee (estimated IDR 1,000,000-2,000,000/year).
data.processingTime: 7-14 working days (e-visa). ITAS conversion after arrival may take additional time.
data.dependents: Yes — spouse, children, parents, siblings (Dec 2025). After main KITAS issued. †Reported by visa agencies; official regulation not yet independently verified.
data.taxImplications: Staying >183 days may trigger tax residency. No E33G-specific tax exemption has been officially published. Consult a tax advisor for foreign-source income treatment.
data.multipleEntry: Initial e-visa is single entry. After converting to ITAS, multiple exit/re-entry is possible via MERP (separate permit with its own fee, obtained after ITAS conversion).
data.recentChanges: Launched April 2024. Policy refinements ongoing. Growing acceptance among immigration authorities.

data.visaCategory: Professional Visit Pass / Pas Lawatan Ikhtisas (Malaysia's digital nomad pass)
data.maxStay: Up to 24 months total (12 months initial + 12 months renewal)
data.extensionRules: Renewable for additional 12 months online without leaving Malaysia.
data.incomeProof: Proof of foreign income source and employment/freelance documentation (minimum 3-month contract)
data.healthInsurance: No official MDEC requirement published. Private healthcare widely available and affordable.
data.remoteWorkAllowed: Yes — can work remotely for foreign employers and freelance for foreign clients
data.localWorkAllowed: No — cannot work for Malaysian companies (Professional Visit Pass, not Employment Pass)
data.applicationFee: MYR 1,000 (~USD 220) main applicant; MYR 500 (~USD 110) per dependent
data.processingTime: Approximately 6-8 weeks per MDEC guidance. Real-world experience ranges 4-12 weeks.
data.dependents: Yes — spouse and dependent children can accompany. Parents are not eligible as DE Rantau dependents.
data.taxImplications: Non-residents (<182 days) pay flat 30% on Malaysian-sourced income. Foreign-sourced income is exempt under Malaysia's FSI exemption (extended to Dec 31, 2036 per Budget 2025, announced October 2024). Consult a tax advisor.
data.recentChanges: Launched October 2022 for tech/digital professionals. Non-tech eligibility expanded June 2024 (DE Rantau Elevate 2024). Maximum stay extended to 24 months total. Income thresholds vary by field (USD 24,000 tech / USD 60,000 non-tech).

data.officialName: Philippine Digital Nomad Visa (Executive Order No. 86, s. 2025)
data.maxStay: 12 months, renewable once (24 months maximum total)
data.extensionRules: Renewable for one additional 12-month period. Maximum 2-year total stay. Renewal procedures per DFA implementing rules.
data.financialRequirement: USD 24,000 minimum annual income from foreign sources (per implementing guidelines; verify against IRR)
data.incomeProof: Proof of remote employment or freelance contracts with foreign clients
data.healthInsurance: Yes — valid international health insurance required throughout entire stay
data.remoteWorkAllowed: Yes — can work for foreign employers and freelance for overseas clients
data.localWorkAllowed: No — cannot work for Philippines-based companies or clients
data.applicationFee: Estimated USD 200-300 (varies by country of residence). Official fee schedule pending IRR publication.
data.dependents: Not yet confirmed for initial program. Check DFA implementing rules for updates.
data.taxImplications: EO 86 contains no tax provisions. DNV holders are expected to be treated as non-resident aliens (foreign-source income likely not taxed), but no BIR guidance has been published confirming this. Consult a Philippine tax advisor.
data.multipleEntry: Yes — multiple entry privileges during visa validity
data.recentChanges: EO 86 signed April 24, 2025, effective May 5, 2025. Pilot phase began June 2025. Dual eligibility requirement: applicant's home country must (1) offer a similar visa to Filipino nationals AND (2) have a Philippine Foreign Service Post. Procedures being refined.
